applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations shown on electrical plan
findings.comment: Transformer pad clearances to buildings are not documented with dimensions on the plans. Access door orientation and confined space conditions cannot be determined from the electrical plan. If any transformer pads utilize reduced 3-foot clearances to brick/masonry buildings, documentation must show: (1) written Austin Energy Design approval, (2) verification that location is not in confined space, (3) confirmation of 10-foot minimum clearance to windows/doors/ducts, (4) 15-foot vertical clearance to windows/doors/ducts, and (5) 3-hour fire rating certification. No such documentation is present.

Transformer equipment type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified on the electrical plan. Windows, doors, and ventilating ducts on adjacent buildings are not clearly identified relative to transformer pad locations. The 12-foot horizontal clearance requirement from windows/doors/ducts when located less than 12 feet from grade cannot be verified without equipment type specification and clear documentation of window/door locations, their heights, and lateral separation distances.

Transformer pad access door orientation and location (hot-stick use area) are not indicated on the electrical plan. Without identifying which side of each transformer pad is the access door and which direction it faces, the 10-foot clearance requirement to open area or adjacent structures cannot be verified for each individual pad.

Transformer pad access door orientation and confined space conditions are not documented. No cross-section drawings are provided showing whether any transformer locations face confined spaces (niches, vaults, or enclosed areas on 3+ sides). The 15-foot hot-stick use area clearance requirement for confined spaces cannot be verified without this information.

No clearance dimensions are shown between transformer pads and gas service lines on the utility plan. Gas line pressure specifications (less than 60 psi vs. 60 psi and over) that would trigger different clearance requirements (24 inches vs. 36 inches) are not provided. Minimum clearance compliance cannot be verified without dimensioned distances and gas pressure data.

Minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from other underground utilities (except gas, fuel, steam) is not dimensioned on the utility plans. Clearances from storm drain, water lines, and wastewater lines to transformer pad locations are not documented with specific measurements, preventing verification of compliance.

The plans do not clearly document whether any AE underground facilities are located over or under other utility lines, or whether any customer buildings/foundations/structures are installed over AE underground facilities. Cross-section drawings showing vertical relationships between transformer electrical conduits and other utilities are not provided.

applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations with overhead structures or enclosed areas
findings.comment: No cross-section drawings are provided showing vertical clearances from transformer pad locations to any overhead structures, building eaves, parking garage overhangs, or enclosed areas. Plan note on Sheet 21 indicates potential niche/enclosed areas and overhead structures in the development, but no detailed cross-sections demonstrating vertical clearance compliance are included in the submitted plan set.

Transformer equipment specifications do not indicate whether equipment is oil-filled or dry-type. Grading plan shows general drainage direction around the site but does not specifically document drainage flow direction around transformer pad locations. For oil-filled equipment, liquid flow must be directed away from buildings, but this cannot be verified without equipment specifications and explicit drainage flow documentation at each transformer location.

Transformer easement boundaries and widths are not shown on the electrical or utility plans. No dimensions or specifications are provided for transformer equipment easements required for Austin Energy accessibility and maintenance. Easement width adequacy cannot be verified against Austin Energy Design requirements.

Transformer pad dimensions are not shown on the electrical plan (pads are drawn as unmarked cross-hatched rectangles). Service type (single-phase or three-phase) is not specified for any transformer. No reference callouts to Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets are provided. Transformer pad size and specification cannot be verified as matching AE Design-approved details for the specified service type and electrical load.

applicableAreas: Transformer Pads 4 and 5 (southeast and east-central areas)
findings.comment: Transformer Pads 4 and 5 are located approximately 5-10 feet from parking/drive areas based on visual analysis. If within 4 feet of parking or vehicle routes, 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal bollards are required per AE Design equipment pad details. No bollard details or specifications are shown on the plans. Distance to parking/circulation areas must be precisely dimensioned to determine bollard requirement, and if required, bollard locations and spacing must be documented to ensure equipment door access is maintained.
